Core semantic audit of the SAIPEN engine at source_head 6c6e2a457125, scope: the core-unit evidence gate and the session's own validator/intake work. One reproduced finding.

IMP-001 [P3] [LOGIC_ERROR] [reproduced] [ticket]
expected: `saipen core_unit evidence` (and `--fresh`) either cites a PASS record for the current tree or reports a real gate failure; a run should complete against a stable subject.
actual: when a SIBLING process edits a tracked file inside the same working tree DURING the family run, tree_fingerprint (core_unit.py:176) after the copy no longer equals the copy's fingerprint, so _evidence (core_unit.py:1047) returns ok:false 'the working tree changed after the family's copy was taken' and the record is not cited. `--fresh` cannot help because the drift happens within the run window, not from a reused record; the only recovery is to wait for the sibling to settle and rerun (observed 4+ times this session, e.g. tools/saipen_engine/audit_inbox.py and tools/test_audit_2026_08_28_all3.py flipping mid-run at 18:11-18:21). T-1479 fixed the .saipen copy race and T-1483 excluded tool caches, but neither covers a concurrent editor of the TESTED source files.
evidence: core_unit.py:1035-1060 recomputes tree_fingerprint after write_record and fails closed on any inequality; the two flipping files were confirmed by a snapshot diff of the fingerprint file set taken immediately before and after a run (diff showed exactly those two paths' hashes changing). No isolation (copy-to-temp-and-run-from-there, or a fingerprint-stable retry loop) exists for the source subject the way it does for .saipen.
action: ticket -- consider running the family from an immutable snapshot copy (fingerprint the copy, run inside it) or a bounded auto-retry when post-run drift is detected and the pre/post delta is outside the ticket's own edits, so a busy multi-session tree does not force manual serialization. Not a correctness hole in the gate (it fails safe), a usability/throughput one.
